long_biography.plain_text:
Computacenter grew by helping large organisations source, integrate and manage workplace technology rather than by creating a single software product. Philip Hulme and Peter Ogden established the company in 1981, combining hardware and software supply with infrastructure and onsite services. That model produced Hulme’s principal wealth and developed into an international technology-services group.

Beyond the group, Hulme links investment experience with institution building. The 2016 honours citation also identifies him as a co-founder of Dealogic and the Hadley Trust, reflecting activity in financial-data technology and philanthropy. Through the Hadley Projects Fund, which he chairs, his current public role is governance and charitable stewardship; at Computacenter, it is non-executive rather than day-to-day management.
